traceability.notes:
The 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING story defines cross-cutting requirements for clear, specific, and consistent error messages across all traceability-related ESLint rules, including severity conventions and graceful handling of edge cases.
Based on the implementation and tests: - All relevant rules define meta.messages using the exact patterns described in the story (functionName, missing, details, path/storyPath/reqId placeholders). - Error messages are specific and actionable, instructing the developer what is wrong and how to fix it (e.g., add @story/@req, fix file path, correct formats), with ESLint suggestions provided where appropriate (notably for require-story-annotation and branch autofixes). - Tests for each rule explicitly reference this story and its REQ-ERROR-* requirements and assert both messageId and data payloads, confirming that errors include precise context (function name, requirement ID, file path) and adhere to the documented conventions. - src/index.ts encodes the required severity mapping (errors vs warnings) and uses it in the exported ESLint configs, satisfying the severity aspect of the story. - Edge cases such as missing location information, malformed configuration, or filesystem failures are handled gracefully and surfaced as diagnostics instead of uncaught exceptions, with dedicated tests validating this behavior. - The dedicated tests/rules/error-reporting.test.ts exercises the enhanced error reporting for require-story-annotation, ensuring that the template, data fields, and suggestions are wired correctly.
All acceptance criteria and enumerated requirements (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC, REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT, REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY, REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY, plus REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) are implemented and verified by passing automated tests. Therefore this story is fully implemented and the assessment status is PASSED.
